rich_summary: On the tenth day of the Kurukshetra war, the armies of the Kauravas and Pandavas collide in a brutal struggle centered on Bhishma and Arjuna. The battlefield becomes a whirlpool of slaughter, the ground soaked with blood. Though riddled with arrows and still killing thousands, Bhishma finally faces Arjuna’s relentless assault. Surrounded and pierced from every side, the grandsire is struck down and falls from his chariot just before sunset, yet his body remains suspended on a bed of arrows without touching the earth. Possessing the boon of choosing the moment of his death, he refuses to die during the inauspicious southern solstice and resolves to wait for the northern one. As sages in swan form witness his vow, both armies react with shock—Pandavas rejoice, while the Kurus fall into grief and confusion—marking a decisive turning point in the war.

highlight_spans.why: The opening establishes the ferocity of the tenth day's battle and the armies rallying around Bhishma.
Describes Bhishma continuing to fight despite mortal wounds and the massive scale of destruction around him.
Captures the dramatic moment of Bhishma’s fall from his chariot as cries rise from heaven and earth.
Highlights Bhishma’s extraordinary vow to postpone death until the auspicious northern solstice, demonstrating his yogic control and heroic resolve.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhishma falling from his chariot at sunset, his body suspended above the ground by countless arrows forming a bed beneath him while warriors watch in shock.
The battlefield swirling like a vortex of clashing armies, the earth soaked red as Bhishma and Arjuna face each other amid flying arrows.
Mystic swan‑formed sages descending from the sky to circle the wounded Bhishma lying serenely on his bed of arrows.
